long_biography.plain_text:
Industrialist Claudio Terruzzi became interested in photocatalysis after seeing self-cleaning sanitary ware during a visit to Japan. At Global Engineering, he pursued its use in paints, cement and other building surfaces. A patent names him as the inventor of a cement paint incorporating a catalyst designed to oxidise pollutants in light and air. The company's early applications included a road in Segrate.

Motorcycle racing also occupied a substantial part of his life. After competing in enduro, he became an official Honda rider and contested the Paris-Dakar rally three times. He finished fifth in 1988, when his teammate Edi Orioli won. Years later, he organised a gathering of former Italian national-team riders to honour enduro champion Augusto Taiocchi.

confidence.reason: Corporate account and patent identify the technical work; specialist race history and national federation establish sustained competition and the later reunion. Identity limitation caps the pair.
